scope: The same ten artifacts reviewed by x-triage-bad, using their current paths after the prior local moves. This review performs no sample moves or label changes.

elevated_findings.description: Docker exec launches shell fork bomb
Node launch attempts unbounded buffer retention

readability_and_accuracy.problem: A local PHP formatter config was reported as command-and-control/endpoint/php with a contacts PHP endpoint description.
readability_and_accuracy.fix: Removed the .php-substring C2 heuristic from the package analyzer. Actual URL strings remain available. A structured scripts.* URL-reference trait records PHP resource paths without claiming contact or C2; local paths, query-only .php values and .phpdata near misses are excluded.

readability_and_accuracy.problem: CCXT test_future.py inherited Python standard-library identity solely from its basename. Numbered p-1 through p-10 findings also hid the observed filenames from their descriptions.
readability_and_accuracy.fix: Relocated ten basename matchers to metadata/filename/source with descriptive IDs and names. Preserved matcher, type/platform scope and notable severity. Removed their membership in the stdlib identity directory instead of carrying filename-only evidence into its consumer.

readability_and_accuracy.problem: A baseline context finding claimed known benign loader status.
readability_and_accuracy.fix: Renamed it python-loader-or-stub-context and described its indicators without a safety verdict. Its conditions are otherwise retained.

readability_and_accuracy.problem: A text fragment resembling a Next/Nuxt import claimed that code uses an established web framework.
readability_and_accuracy.fix: Retired the redundant uses-web-framework-b text rule. Parser-backed metadata/import/npm/next and Nuxt import findings remain. No direct rule consumers referenced the retired ID.

missing_behavior.description: A parsed spawn call supplies detached:true in its options object. The observation occurs in the actual CCXT playground runner; it describes child-process configuration, not persistence or authorization.

future_attack_coverage.change: Detects direct unconditional self-piping shell functions by comparing the declared function and both recursive callees. Renaming the function does not evade the rule; a pipeline to a different consumer, a stopping branch, comments and echo text do not qualify.

Detects JavaScript/TypeScript tight while(true) and for(;;) allocation loops, with or without a block. A neighboring array declaration must bind the actual push receiver. The entire body retains Buffer allocations, with no break, eviction, conditional or pacing statement. Custom push objects, missing receivers and inert source strings are negative controls.
Accepts absolute Docker/shell paths, combined -lc/-ec interpreter flags and timeout --signal variants while preserving explicit Docker exec positioning.

Supports absolute Docker paths, shell flags, Node --eval, spacing and block bodies. Requires an array-declaration prefix and a complete constrained allocation-loop ending. Commands that replace the shell with exec echo, loops with break and source-looking string bodies are rejected. The description explicitly describes an attempt; it does not assert successful runtime allocation.

verification.atomscan_local_engine_build: passed; temporary scan manifest patched to the local cleave checkout, original scan checkout and lockfile unchanged

full_validation.status: blocked by pre-existing and concurrent repository issues
full_validation.details: Initial validation had 53 issues. verification.formatting: git diff --check and Rust formatting check for package_json.rs passed

limits: Static analysis only: no package scripts, bomb payloads, network requests or sample programs were executed.

The new source memory rule intentionally requires a fresh neighboring array binding and a tight loop body. It does not model arbitrary interprocedural allocation/retention or all possible memory-exhaustion mechanisms.

The shell memory rule still recognizes a constrained literal program shape; it does not prove every runtime variable relationship or successful allocation. The new source rule binds the array receiver structurally.

The recursive-function rule covers source function bodies. The existing handoff rules retain coverage of the classic inline colon-function payload; arbitrary dynamic shell reconstruction is outside this review.
Known flow and embedded-source limitations remain in the reports; no evaluation-deadline gaps occurred.

The local binaries include the analyzer correction through a temporary dependency override. Publishing/merging the cleave change and rolling the upstream scan dependency is outside this task; the patch and build config preserve the reviewable change.
